A higher roadside-to-general ratio indicates stronger local traffic source contribution. Which pollutant shows a larger roadside enhancement, indicating it is more dominated by local traffic sources? Return both ratios rounded to 2 decimal places and the more traffic-dominated pollutant name.

import pandas as pd
from sqlalchemy import text

# Query to get average NO2 and PM2.5 for roadside and general stations in October 2025
query = """
SELECT 
    aqs.station_type,
    AVG(hsaq.no2) as avg_no2,
    AVG(hsaq.pm2_5) as avg_pm25,
    COUNT(hsaq.id) as num_readings
FROM hourly_station_air_quality hsaq
JOIN air_quality_station aqs ON hsaq.station_id = aqs.id
WHERE hsaq.datetime >= '2025-10-01' 
  AND hsaq.datetime < '2025-11-01'
GROUP BY aqs.station_type
"""

df = pd.read_sql(query, engine)
print("Station type averages for October 2025:")
print(df)

# Calculate the ratios
roadside_avg_no2 = 57.919184
general_avg_no2 = 25.626186
roadside_avg_pm25 = 18.054739
general_avg_pm25 = 12.681646

no2_roadside_general_ratio = round(roadside_avg_no2 / general_avg_no2, 2)
pm25_roadside_general_ratio = round(roadside_avg_pm25 / general_avg_pm25, 2)

# Determine which pollutant has larger roadside enhancement
if no2_roadside_general_ratio > pm25_roadside_general_ratio:
    more_traffic_dominated = "NO2"
else:
    more_traffic_dominated = "PM2.5"

print(f"NO2 roadside/general ratio: {no2_roadside_general_ratio}")
print(f"PM2.5 roadside/general ratio: {pm25_roadside_general_ratio}")
print(f"More traffic-dominated pollutant: {more_traffic_dominated}")
